_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); integrated oil and gas signals

pit_profile.why: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business is energy, involving exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas, manufacture of petroleum products and transportation and sale of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products'; 'The oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses are fundamentally commodity businesses. This means ExxonMobil’s operations and earnings may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among its risk factors, 'increased competitiveness of alternative energy sources that have so far generally not been competitive with oil and gas without the benefit of government subsidies or mandates' and 'Due to concern over the risk of climate change, a number of countries have adopted, or are considering the adoption of, regulatory frameworks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions', which 'could make our products more expensive and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shifting hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon sources such as natural gas' (its own FY2009 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oil and gas producer, so the alternative-energy and climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business is energy, involving exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas, manufacture of petroleum products and transportation and sale of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products'; 'The oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses are fundamentally commodity businesses. This means ExxonMobil’s operations and earnings may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among its risk factors, 'increased competitiveness of alternative energy sources that have so far generally not been competitive with oil and gas without the benefit of government subsidies or mandates' and 'Due to concern over the risk of climate change, a number of countries have adopted, or are considering the adoption of, regulatory frameworks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions', which 'could make our products more expensive and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shifting hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon sources such as natural gas' (its own FY2009 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oil and gas producer, so the alternative-energy and climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 2.62x; +57% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.55; conservative 2yr +1%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -52.5%/yr (worst year FY00-FY09, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +20.0%/yr (Q3 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +20.0%/yr (FY00-FY09 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +53.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY00-FY09); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: XOM (retrospective, 2011-01-07) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.62x (88.1% downside to Bear $9 / +33.6% upside to Bull $101) | Adj composite 3.25 vs market 2.70: gap +0.55 [UNDERVALUED] | +57% above the EPP floor $48 (12x FY10E $4.01) | Conservative 2-yr case: +0.9% total (+0.4%/yr) | At 18.9x FY10E the 15% hurdle price $100 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; oil-equivalent production +20.5% in Q3 2010, forward revenues +15.8% (no Q4 2010 revenue guide, Q3 2010 revenue as reported); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
